mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its previous month's value by more than 0.25 percentage points
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative returns occur when FEDFUNDS crosses above prior month by >0.25pp (t-test p > 0.05); or SPX 20d returns remain non-negative despite qualifying FEDFUNDS spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 50,000 over the preceding month, sustained for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, no significant positive 20d returns occur after qualifying PAYEMS spikes (t-test p > 0.05); or SPX returns revert to negative within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior quarter's level predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak manufacturing demand reduces investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 10% from its prior quarter average
failure_condition: No significant negative 60d returns occur after INDPRO contractions (Rank IC > 0.05); or SPX returns remain non-negative despite multiple such contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) of ≥ 0.5% coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumers shift spending to durable goods, signaling resilient demand.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 0.5% month-over-month for the first time in three months
failure_condition: Over 60 days, no statistically significant positive 20d returns occur after qualifying CPIAUCSL declines (p > 0.05); or SPX returns remain flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 2% trigger a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates further rate cuts by the Fed.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60d returns occur when CPIAUCSL stays below 2% for ≥ 3 months (t-test p > 0.05); or Fed raises rates during this window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.5% for the first time in 4 months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market uncertainty intensifies.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% for the first time in the last 4 months
failure_condition: In regimes with low inflation, no significant negative returns occur after UNRATE spikes (p > 0.05); or SPX returns revert to positive within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (HOUST) by at least 5% and 10% respectively over the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual supply-demand pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥ 5% AND HOUST decreases by ≥ 10% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative 20d returns occur after qualifying dual declines (Rank IC > 0.05); or one of the proxies recovers strongly while the other remains weak.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as risk aversion declines and credit spreads narrow.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In non-easing regimes or when FEDFUNDS re-enters tightening, no significant positive 60d returns occur (t-test p > 0.05); or returns revert to negative within 12 months.
